title: State and government

blocks.heading: State and government
blocks.text: A state is an enduring political organisation with territory, population and governing institutions; a government exercises public power through those institutions. Rules, representation and accountability influence whose needs affect public decisions. A change of government does not necessarily create a different state.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Constitution
blocks.text: A constitution is the fundamental rules establishing how a state is organised, how public power is exercised and the rights recognised. It differs from an ordinary policy and requires implementation and accountability to influence lived access.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Authority
blocks.text: Authority is recognised legitimacy to make decisions or exercise power within a specified role. An authorised officer can have limited resources; formal authority differs from the practical capacity to influence outcomes.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Power
blocks.text: Power is the capacity to influence actions or outcomes; it can exist without recognised legitimate authority. A person may exert influence through resources or pressure without holding the authorised role.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Representation
blocks.text: Representation is acting or speaking on behalf of others in decision-making. Meaningful representation needs communication and accountability to those represented, rather than presence alone.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Delegation
blocks.text: Delegation assigns a task or decision responsibility to another person or body within defined limits. Clear limits, resources and reporting matter; assigning work without means to perform it may fail.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Election
blocks.text: An election is a process for choosing representatives or office holders through voting. Fair choice also depends on accessible participation, information and credible procedures.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Voting
blocks.text: Voting is expressing a choice in an election or collective decision under its rules. A vote records a choice, while representation concerns subsequent decisions on others’ behalf.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: Suggest an accountability arrangement for an invented elected committee whose members do not report spending decisions to residents. Publish usable records and hold an accessible reporting meeting with a route to question decisions. This addresses missing information and feedback.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect institutions to National Development Plans (2.2), public services and Development (1.1). Separate rules, resources, implementation and outcomes; fictional examples are not allegations about real officials.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
